ask: Compare Calendly, Cal.com and SavvyCal on team scheduling - pricing pages and help docs only. 20 minutes tops.
notes: Tight time box and fixed source kinds. Quick track fits. The intake must not grow the scope (no reviews, no changelogs) and should keep the questions to one or two.
message:
**Goal:** compare Calendly, Cal.com and SavvyCal on team scheduling, so you can decide what to build or buy.

**Found:**
- Rivals: Calendly, Cal.com, SavvyCal (from your message).
- Sources: pricing pages and help docs only, no sign-ins (from your message).
- Time limit: 20 minutes (from your message), so I will run the quick version.
- Main output: a comparison sheet, Excel and CSV, with a source link on every yes cell.
- Where it lands: `research/team-scheduling/` in this folder. Nothing is published or sent.
- Web check worked: Calendly's pricing page shows Free $0, Standard $10, Teams $16 per seat, with round robin on Teams only.

**Track:** quick, because you set 20 minutes and two source kinds (pricing, help docs).

Still open after reading your files: who this is for, and what you are deciding.

**Done means:**
- Excel and CSV sheet saved in `research/team-scheduling/`.
- Each of the 3 rivals has at least 5 rows read.
- Every yes cell links to that rival's own page.
- Every "no rival has it" claim is searched on all 3 sites.
- The brief ends with a ranked module list citing sheet rows.

Full brief: `loop-runs/product-research-loop-20261126-035141/brief.md`

About 20 minutes and 8 helper agents, within a budget of 20 minutes.

1. What are you building or deciding, in one line?
   Recommended: a team scheduling module for our product, and which features to build first.
   Why it matters: it sets whether the sheet ends in a build order or a buy decision.

2. Who uses it every day, and who pays?
   Recommended: a sales team lead who sets up round-robin booking; the company pays per seat.
   Why it matters: the persona only ranks the modules; it never removes a row from the sheet.

3. How bold should the brief be?
   Recommended: both, with at least 3 ideas no rival has, after the catch-up modules.
   Why it matters: it decides whether the ranked list leads with catching up or with new ideas.

Reply with your answers, or just "go" to use the defaults.
